_doc: Deep dives (view command): when one cause takes a big share of agent time, a focused second analysis runs. It triggers when the matched agent time is at least min_s seconds AND (at least min_share_pct of agent time OR at least or_min_s seconds). 'match' (regex, case-insensitive) is tried on each timeline leaf's command signature ('what'), the run it waited for ('waited_for') and, for poll/deploy/network leaves, the agent's description; 'exclude' drops leaves whose command only reads or edits text about the cause (grep deploy, cat deploy.md). Every leaf of the listed 'segments' counts too. Calls matching 'run' (or segments.deploy_parts) start the thing; poll_wait calls wait for it; the rest are checks. Calls of one session less than episode_gap_s apart form one episode (one deploy and its waiting); episodes starting less than back_to_back_s after the previous one ended are back to back. 'checks' read the project's files on disk (today's state); a check with 'platforms' runs only when one of those platforms was seen in the calls, one with 'unless_platforms' only when none of them was: type file_has (ok when any of the files matches regex), order (bad when 'first' comes before 'then' in a file; when the 'then' line also matches 'minor_if' the finding is only 'minor': listed with the 'minor' text, its tip not raised), exists (bad when none of 'need' sits next to the file or at the repo root). 'tips' fire on computed facts: cond is 'fact >= number'. The 'brief' lines become OUT/<name>.deepdive-<id>.md, the prompt for the subagent that does the AI part ({...} are filled from the facts). Its notes come back in notes.json under 'deepdive:<id>'. A tip with 'same_as' is left out when that slice rule (rules/segments.json) already shows on the page. With 'same_as_share' ('fact / fact') that rule's estimate uses this measured share instead of its fixed saving_fraction (only ever lower).

deep_dives.title: Deploy waits

tip.title: Cache the package store in the image build
tip.why: Without a cache mount every image build downloads and installs all dependencies again, even when only source code changed. Cache mounts persist only on a long-lived builder (a self-hosted Coolify server); on a fresh hosted worker such as Cloud Build they stay empty, so the check is skipped there and cloudbuild-cache applies.
tip.source: Docker docs, Optimize cache usage in builds: https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/optimize/

checks.ok: Lockfiles are copied before the sources in {files}
checks.bad: Sources are copied before the dependency install: {files}
checks.minor: Sources are copied before the install ({files}), but the install has a cache mount, so a rerun only relinks packages: a small gain, not raised as advice

tip.title: Copy lockfiles first, install, then copy the sources
tip.why: COPY . . before the install step changes that layer on every source edit, so the install step runs again on every deploy (a cache mount keeps the downloads, not the install itself).
tip.after:
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .   (pnpm workspace: COPY pnpm-lock.yaml ./, RUN pnpm fetch, COPY . ., RUN pnpm install --offline)
tip.source: Docker docs, Optimize cache usage in builds (order your layers): https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/optimize/ ; pnpm docs, pnpm fetch: https://pnpm.io/cli/fetch

tip.title: Add a .dockerignore
tip.why: Without it the whole directory (node_modules, .git, build output) is sent as build context on every deploy and invalidates COPY layers.

checks.ok: Cloud Build reuses an image cache ({files})
checks.bad: {files} builds without --cache-from or a kaniko cache

tip.title: Reuse the previous image as build cache in Cloud Build
tip.why: Cloud Build starts each build on a fresh worker; without --cache-from (or kaniko's cache) every layer is rebuilt.
tip.after: docker pull IMAGE:latest || true; docker build --cache-from IMAGE:latest -t IMAGE .  (or kaniko with --cache=true)
tip.source: Google Cloud docs, Speeding up your builds: https://cloud.google.com/build/docs/optimize-builds/speeding-up-builds

tips.title: Wait on each deploy with one blocking call
tips.why: Each status check is a model turn that re-reads the whole context; {checks_per_deploy} checks per deploy here. One call that polls inside the shell and exits on success or failure turns them into one turn.
tips.evidence: {episodes} deploys, {status_calls} status checks and poll calls, {checks_per_deploy} per deploy
tips.before: check status, sleep, check status … ({checks_per_deploy} turns per deploy)
tips.after: one call that waits: the platform's own wait (gh run watch --exit-status, gh pr checks --watch --fail-fast) or a script that polls until finished or failed and exits non-zero on failure; run it in the background (or as a Monitor) and act on its end notice
tips.source: GitHub CLI manual: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run_watch ; Claude Code docs, Tools reference (Bash run_in_background, Monitor): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference

tips.title: Batch fixes: {back_to_back} deploys started right after the previous one
tips.why: A deploy that starts less than {back_to_back_min} min after the previous one ended usually ships one more small fix; each costs a full build and rollout ({episode_p50}).
tips.evidence: {back_to_back} of {episodes} deploys started within {back_to_back_min} min of the previous deploy's end
tips.same_as_share_text: {back_to_back} of {episodes} deploys started within {back_to_back_min} min of the previous deploy's end

tips.title: Run long deploy commands in the background
tips.why: {foreground_long} deploy commands blocked the agent for more than a minute in the foreground; a foreground Bash call waits up to its timeout (2 min by default) before it is moved to the background. A background run reports its end, so the agent can keep working.
tips.evidence: {foreground_long} foreground deploy calls over 60 s, longest {longest_run}
tips.before: deploy in the foreground, the agent waits
tips.after: deploy with run_in_background; continue; act on the end notice
tips.source: Claude Code docs, Tools reference (timeout and run_in_background): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference

brief: You are a subagent started by the analyse-bottleneck skill. Deploy-related work took {total} = {share} of agent time (trigger: {trigger}). Find where that time goes and what would cut it.
1. Find the deploy path: the commands above, the deploy script or CI config, the Dockerfile(s) and the platform ({platforms}).

2. Measure instead of guessing. Read the platform's own records of recent deploys if you can reach them read-only (its deploy history or build logs: start, end, steps). Split a typical deploy into queue, image build (which steps), push, and rollout or health check.
3. Name the 1-3 biggest avoidable parts and the concrete change for each (file:line or setting), with an estimate that traces to numbers you measured or to the facts above.
Rules: read-only. No deploys, restarts, config or file changes. Never print secrets, tokens or env values. If something cannot be measured, say so in the note instead of guessing.
## Return only this JSON (at most 3 notes)
